Dirichlet's Test

A wobbling series gets tamed by a sinking weight in this scene. Two ingredients meet and produce convergence.

The partial sums of the sine terms wobble around but stay trapped inside a fixed fence. Multiply them by weights that sink to 0. The wobble gets pressed flatter and flatter until the series converges. The test's exact conditions are in the formulas below.

For example, a ⚽ ball bounces around inside a fence and never escapes. Push it more and more gently, and its wandering dies down until it settles.

∑k=1Nsin⁡(kx)=sin⁡Nx2 sin⁡(N+1)x2sin⁡x2,∣∑k=1Nsin⁡(kx)∣≤1∣sin⁡(x/2)∣\sum_{k=1}^{N}\sin(kx) = \frac{\sin\frac{Nx}{2}\,\sin\frac{(N+1)x}{2}}{\sin\frac{x}{2}},\quad \left|\sum_{k=1}^{N}\sin(kx)\right| \le \frac{1}{|\sin(x/2)|}k=1∑N​sin(kx)=sin2x​sin2Nx​sin2(N+1)x​​,​k=1∑N​sin(kx)​≤∣sin(x/2)∣1​
∑n=1∞sin⁡(nx)n=π−x2,x∈(0,2π)\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sin(nx)}{n} = \frac{\pi-x}{2},\quad x \in (0, 2\pi)n=1∑∞​nsin(nx)​=2π−x​,x∈(0,2π)

Show that the Leibniz alternating series test is a corollary of Dirichlet's test.

∣∑n=1N(−1)n∣≤1\left|\sum_{n=1}^{N} (-1)^n\right| \le 1​n=1∑N​(−1)n​≤1

Applying Dirichlet's test to the pair (an,bn)(a_n, b_n)(an​,bn​) yields convergence of ∑n=1∞(−1)nbn\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (-1)^n b_n∑n=1∞​(−1)nbn​ at once — the alternating series test is Dirichlet's test in the case an=(−1)na_n = (-1)^nan​=(−1)n.
